title: Extraction and Ghost
premise: Lena Ashgrove, a former compliance analyst turned whistle-blower hiding under four identities, is contacted by a stranger named Marek who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of. He offers her the one thing she wants, proof that will clear her name, in exchange for helping him extract his brother Tomas, a central-bank defector carrying evidence of a market-rigging scheme, out of Vienna before Frankfurt markets open. Lena realizes mid-operation that Tomas may be bait set by the very syndicate she exposed years ago, and that Marek's debt story is a lever to use her. In the end, Lena chooses love over duty — burning her last safe identity to get Tomas and the evidence across the border, exposing the syndicate at the cost of her old life, and finally sleeping through the night under her real name.
about_author: Ada Underhill is the pen name of a former financial journalist who spent a decade covering regulatory scandals across Europe before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside extraordinary machinery, drawing on the gray zones between loyalty, law, and survival.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. We meet her in Rotterdam under the name 'Ingrid,' running a meticulous, sleepless life of dead drops and burner phones. A small anomaly — a coffee order she never placed arriving at her table — rattles her. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A man called Marek approaches with impossible details: he says she saved his life in Prague three years ago, a night she cannot remember. He leaves an envelope containing a photo of herself she thought was destroyed. Beat: vertigo — her past is not where she buried it.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. He explains the debt: his brother Tomas, a defector inside the European clearing house, holds ledgers proving the Meridian Syndicate rigs settlement flows. He needs Lena's old access codes and instincts. Beat: temptation dressed as obligation.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Walls
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, Vienna. Tomas hides encrypted drives inside a bank archive, terrified, counting hours until a scheduled audit exposes him. He trusts no one, least of all his brother's mysterious contact. Beat: claustrophobic fear.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She maps the extraction window: forty-eight hours, one border crossing, one train. She rehearses routes like a prayer. Beat: cold competence masking terror as she agrees for reasons she won't admit — the proof that can clear her name.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She sheds 'Ingrid' and becomes 'Clara,' meeting Marek in a safehouse above a shuttered cinema. Their chemistry is immediate and dangerous. Beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches Trains
chapters.summary: New POV: Voss, the Syndicate's fixer, arrives in Vienna, reading passenger manifests like scripture. He suspects Tomas but wants whoever comes for him more. Beat: patient menace; the trap begins closing.

chapters.title: Archive Night
chapters.summary: Lena and Tomas POV alternating. First contact with Tomas in the archive stacks goes wrong when an audit team arrives early. Lena improvises, and Tomas sees she's real. Beat: adrenaline, first trust.

chapters.title: What Marek Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She finds a discrepancy in Marek's story — the Prague favor predates her whistle-blowing by a year. Someone fed him her history. Beat: betrayal's first cold draft.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Lena confronts him; he admits he was recruited to recruit her, but insists the debt is real and his feelings are not part of the job. Beat: love against duty, stated plainly for the first time.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. We learn the truth: Tomas is deliberately allowed to run so the Syndicate can identify and destroy the last witness — Lena. The extraction is a designed leak. Beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Danube Route
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Plan B: a cargo barge down the Danube instead of the train. She burns another identity to book passage. Beat: the price of survival made literal — each escape costs a self.

chapters.title: Tomas Breaks
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Cornered by doubt and a Syndicate approach promising amnesty, Tomas nearly takes it. Lena talks him back from the ledge with her own story of what surrender cost her. Beat: fragile solidarity.

chapters.title: Midnight Loading
chapters.summary: Lena and Marek POV. The barge loading goes smoothly — too smoothly. Lena spots Voss's surveillance pattern and realizes they're being herded. Beat: dread crystallizing into certainty.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the border checkpoint, agents sweep the barge. Marek draws them off and is taken. Lena must choose: rescue him or move Tomas. Beat: the book's moral hinge.

chapters.title: Duty
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She chooses the mission, hating herself, moving Tomas through reed marshes toward Slovakia while sirens rise behind her. Beat: duty as a wound.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Voss interrogates Marek, offering him Lena's location in exchange for Tomas's drives. Marek gives up a false route instead. Beat: loyalty proven under pain.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena brokers a desperate trade through a sympathetic EU auditor: the ledgers' public release in exchange for Marek and safe passage. Beat: turning the bait into the weapon.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock in Frankfurt
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. As markets open, the ledger data hits regulators and newswires; Meridian's positions unravel in real time. Voss receives orders to make everything disappear — including witnesses. Beat: chaos as catharsis.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Final confrontation at the river dock: Voss versus Lena and Marek. Tomas's testimony and the auditor's arrival strip Voss of cover; he retreats rather than die for men already ruined. Beat: survival without triumph.

chapters.title: One Name Left
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Aftermath: hearings begin, Marek recovers, and Lena stands before a microphone using her real name for the first time in years. Beat: inheritance — reclaiming the identity she tried to bury.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, quiet epilogue months later. A small apartment, a door she doesn't double-lock, Tomas teaching, Marek making coffee she actually ordered. She sleeps through the night. Beat: peace earned, not given.
